title: Markdown to HTML
summary: Turn Markdown notes into HTML: headings, paragraphs, emphasis, inline code, lists and code blocks. You’ll walk through strings and slices, return borrowed text, and model a document with an enum.

milestones.title: Escape HTML
milestones.build: `escape` replaces `&`, `<`, `>` and `"` with their HTML entities. Loop over `chars()` and push onto a new `String`.

milestones.title: Headings
milestones.build: `heading` recognises `## Title`: one to six `#`s and a space. It returns the level and a `&str` slice of the line, borrowed rather than copied.

milestones.title: Emphasis and code
milestones.build: `inline` turns `**strong**`, `*em*` and code between backticks into tags and escapes the rest. Walk the text with a `rest` slice, use `find` to look for the closing marker, and call `inline` again for the text between strong or em markers.

milestones.title: Paragraphs and headings
milestones.build: `parse` goes line by line and collects `Block`s. Gather text lines until a blank line or a heading, then push a `Paragraph` of the lines joined with spaces.

milestones.title: Lists
milestones.build: Lines that start with `- ` or `* ` become items of a `List`. A blank line or a text line ends the list. `*so* important` isn’t an item: the `*` has no space after it.

milestones.title: Code blocks
milestones.build: A line starting with three backticks opens a code block, and the next such line closes it. Keep the lines inside exactly as they are. An `Option<…>` for “am I inside a fence?” keeps the state in one place.

milestones.title: Write HTML
milestones.build: `render` turns each block into HTML with a `match`, and `to_html` ties it together. Then convert the sample: `cargo run -- notes.md`.
